The model expresses the human transgene rather than carrying the variant at the endogenous mouse locus, and degeneration is widespread rather than selectively nigral.

nodes.description: In the missense subtype the lesion is a single substitution in the N-terminal amphipathic repeats, which changes the conformational and membrane-binding behaviour of the protein. Most alleles (p.Ala53Thr, p.Glu46Lys, p.His50Gln) accelerate fibril formation, which is why this node feeds the aggregation node. The direction is not uniform: p.Ala30Pro fibrillizes more slowly and p.Gly51Asp and p.Ala53Glu attenuate aggregation in vitro, so the node asserts an altered aggregation propensity, not a uniform increase, and the per-allele direction is recorded on the variants.

evidence.reference_title: Accelerated in vitro fibril formation by a mutant alpha-synuclein linked to early-onset Parkinson disease.
evidence.snippet: Thus, mutation-induced acceleration of alpha-synuclein fibril formation may contribute to the early onset of familial PD.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations associated with familial Parkinson's disease alter the initiation and amplification steps of α-synuclein aggregation.
evidence.snippet: We find that lipid-induced fibril production and surface catalyzed fibril amplification are the processes most strongly affected by these mutations and show that familial mutations can induce dramatic changes in the crucial processes thought to be associated with the initiation and spreading of the aggregation of α-synuclein.

evidence.reference_title: The novel Parkinson's disease linked mutation G51D attenuates in vitro aggregation and membrane binding of α-synuclein, and enhances its secretion and nuclear localization in cells.
evidence.snippet: Our results show that the G51D mutation significantly attenuates α-Syn aggregation in vitro.

genetic_context.description: A heterozygous missense change in the N-terminal membrane-binding region; the effect on aggregation is allele-specific.

nodes.description: The shared downstream step of both branches. Excess or altered alpha-synuclein self-assembles from monomers through soluble oligomers into beta-sheet-rich amyloid fibrils. The oligomeric intermediates, not the mature fibrils, carry most of the toxicity: engineered oligomer-forming variants cause more dopaminergic loss in vivo than fast-fibrillizing ones.
nodes.id: Alpha-Synuclein Oligomerization and Amyloid Fibril Formation

evidence.reference_title: In vivo demonstration that alpha-synuclein oligomers are toxic.
evidence.snippet: The most severe dopaminergic loss in the substantia nigra is observed in animals with the α-syn variants that form oligomers (i.e., E57K and E35K), whereas the α-syn variants that form fibrils very quickly are less toxic.

evidence.reference_title: Neuronal alpha-synucleinopathy with severe movement disorder in mice expressing A53T human alpha-synuclein.
evidence.snippet: These mice demonstrate that A53T alpha-synuclein leads to the formation of toxic filamentous alpha-synuclein neuronal inclusions that cause neurodegeneration.

nodes.id: Alpha-synuclein protein level in blood and brain (SNCA triplication)

evidence.reference_title: Alpha-synuclein in blood and brain from familial Parkinson disease with SNCA locus triplication.
evidence.snippet: Here it is shown that SNCA triplication results in a doubling in the amount of alpha-synuclein protein in blood.

readouts.interpretation: Blood and brain alpha-synuclein level reads out the gene-dosage node directly in multiplication carriers.

nodes.description: Visual hallucinations and psychosis, frequent in SNCA disease, are managed by reducing offending medication and, when needed, a Parkinson-safe atypical antipsychotic that does not worsen parkinsonism. Typical neuroleptics and other dopamine blockers are avoided.
nodes.id: Antipsychotic Management of Visual Hallucinations and Psychosis

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal dominant Parkinson's disease caused by SNCA duplications.
evidence.snippet: Hallucinations were the only feature present significantly more often than not (χ2 test, p<0.01) in these patients.

nodes.description: Slowness of movement, a cardinal sign and part of the diagnostic criterion for parkinsonism.

evidence.reference_title: Distinct clinical and neuropathological features of G51D SNCA mutation cases compared with SNCA duplication and H50Q mutation.
evidence.snippet: Examination revealed hypomimia, micrographia, bilateral resting hand tremor, asymmetrical bradykinesia and rigidity with parkinsonian gait and reduced arm swing.

nodes.description: Alpha-synuclein pathology affects peripheral autonomic neurons, producing sympathetic denervation of the heart that is demonstrable by reduced cardiac MIBG uptake and by absent tyrosine-hydroxylase immunostaining in the myocardium at autopsy. It is documented in p.Glu46Lys carriers, including asymptomatic ones, and underlies the orthostatic hypotension of the dysautonomia.

evidence.reference_title: Cardiac sympathetic denervation in symptomatic and asymptomatic carriers of the E46K mutation in the α synuclein gene.
evidence.snippet: There was a complete absence of tyrosine hydroxylase immunostaining in the myocardium of the two autopsied cases.

nodes.description: Where aggregate burden extends beyond the brainstem into neocortex and limbic regions, as it characteristically does in triplication and in the p.Glu46Lys and p.Gly51Asp subtypes, it produces the dementia, visual hallucinations and psychiatric features that distinguish SNCA disease from typical sporadic Parkinson disease. Hippocampal CA2/3 neuronal loss is a recurrent feature across multiplication and missense carriers.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal dominant Parkinson's disease caused by SNCA duplications.
evidence.snippet: Our patient and the other reported cases with SNCA duplications had widespread cortical Lewy pathology. Neuronal loss in the hippocampal cornu ammonis 2/3 regions were seen in about half of the autopsied SNCA duplication cases.

nodes.description: Cognitive decline, frequent in SNCA disease and more so than in idiopathic Parkinson disease. It is near-universal in triplication, common in duplication (noted in about half of multiplication probands), and part of the p.Glu46Lys and p.Gly51Asp phenotypes.

evidence.reference_title: A Meta-Analysis of α-Synuclein Multiplication in Familial Parkinsonism.
evidence.snippet: Atypical or more severe clinical courses were described in several patients and dementia was noted in 50.9% of the probands.

evidence.reference_title: The new mutation, E46K, of alpha-synuclein causes Parkinson and Lewy body dementia.
evidence.snippet: We present a Spanish family with autosomal dominant parkinsonism, dementia, and visual hallucinations of variable severity.

nodes.description: Depression, a frequent non-motor feature across SNCA carriers, including duplication carriers, that can precede motor onset.

evidence.reference_title: Distinct clinical and neuropathological features of G51D SNCA mutation cases compared with SNCA duplication and H50Q mutation.
evidence.snippet: At age 69, this British Caucasian presented with resting tremor of the right hand, anxiety and depression.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal dominant Parkinson's disease caused by SNCA duplications.

nodes.description: Autonomic dysfunction, including orthostatic hypotension, which can dominate the early picture and lead to an initial diagnosis of multiple system atrophy; it has a demonstrable peripheral basis in cardiac sympathetic denervation.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal dominant Parkinson's disease caused by SNCA duplications.
evidence.snippet: Our case presented with depression and RBD that preceded parkinsonism, and dysautonomia that led to an initial diagnosis of multiple system atrophy.

nodes.description: Wild-type alpha-synuclein is normally cleared by chaperone-mediated autophagy. The A53T and A30P mutants bind the lysosomal CMA receptor LAMP2A but are not translocated, so they block the pathway for themselves and for other substrates; dopamine-modified alpha-synuclein does the same in sporadic disease. Loss of this degradation route raises the aggregating load and feeds back onto aggregation.
nodes.id: Impaired Chaperone-Mediated Autophagy and Protein Degradation

evidence.reference_title: Impaired degradation of mutant alpha-synuclein by chaperone-mediated autophagy.
evidence.snippet: We found that wild-type alpha-synuclein was selectively translocated into lysosomes for degradation by the chaperone-mediated autophagy pathway.

evidence.reference_title: Dopamine-modified alpha-synuclein blocks chaperone-mediated autophagy.
evidence.snippet: Pathogenic mutants of alpha-syn block lysosomal translocation, impairing their own degradation along with that of other CMA substrates.

nodes.description: Alpha-synuclein is a presynaptic protein, and an increased amount of it impairs neurotransmitter release before any cell loss. Overexpression at the level predicted for multiplication reduces the synaptic vesicle recycling pool and blocks reclustering of vesicles after endocytosis, inhibiting release; this is a physiological deficit that precedes detectable neuropathology. This node captures the earliest, pre-degenerative consequence of raised alpha-synuclein.
nodes.id: Impaired Synaptic Vesicle Recycling and Dopamine Release

evidence.reference_title: Increased expression of alpha-synuclein reduces neurotransmitter release by inhibiting synaptic vesicle reclustering after endocytosis.
evidence.snippet: Increased levels of alpha-synuclein thus produce a specific, physiological defect in synaptic vesicle recycling that precedes detectable neuropathology.

evidence.reference_title: Increased expression of alpha-synuclein reduces neurotransmitter release by inhibiting synaptic vesicle reclustering after endocytosis.
evidence.snippet: the modest overexpression of alpha-synuclein, in the range predicted for gene multiplication and in the absence of overt toxicity, markedly inhibits neurotransmitter release.

nodes.description: In the multiplication subtype the lesion is copy number: three or four copies of the wild-type SNCA locus raise alpha-synuclein mRNA and protein roughly in proportion to dosage. Triplication doubles the protein in blood and brain, and the effect on the aggregated, insoluble fraction is larger than on the soluble pool. This node is the root of the dosage branch; the missense branch starts at the next node. The bound phospholipid-binding molecular function represents alpha-synuclein's normal membrane activity; the INCREASED modifier marks the raised amount of the otherwise-normal protein, not a higher per-molecule lipid affinity.

evidence.reference_title: Alpha-synuclein in blood and brain from familial Parkinson disease with SNCA locus triplication.
evidence.snippet: Here it is shown that SNCA triplication results in a doubling in the amount of alpha-synuclein protein in blood. Examination of brain tissue showed a doubling in the level of SNCA message.

evidence.reference_title: Alpha-synuclein in blood and brain from familial Parkinson disease with SNCA locus triplication.
evidence.snippet: However, at the protein level in brain, there was a greater effect on deposition of aggregated forms into insoluble fractions than on net expression of soluble alpha-synuclein.

evidence.reference_title: Parkinson's disease induced pluripotent stem cells with triplication of the α-synuclein locus.
evidence.snippet: When these cells are differentiated into midbrain dopaminergic neurons, those from the patient produce double the amount of α-synuclein protein as neurons from the unaffected relative, precisely recapitulating the cause of Parkinson's disease in these individuals.

experimental_models.description: Patient-derived dopaminergic neurons reproduce the doubling of alpha-synuclein that the triplication causes.

genetic_context.description: Duplication or triplication of the wild-type locus; the protein is normal and its amount is increased.

nodes.description: Treatment does not differ from sporadic Parkinson disease. Levodopa with carbidopa or benserazide is the mainstay, and the response is generally good across the dominant genetic forms, although in triplication and p.Gly51Asp disease it is less durable and motor complications appear early. The response is symptomatic: levodopa restores striatal dopaminergic transmission and does not touch the synuclein lesion.

evidence.reference_title: G51D α-synuclein mutation causes a novel parkinsonian-pyramidal syndrome.
evidence.snippet: G51D was associated with an unusual PD phenotype characterized by early disease onset, moderate response to levodopa, rapid progression leading to loss of autonomy and death within a few years

nodes.description: The parkinsonism responds well to levodopa, as in sporadic disease and across the dominant genetic forms.

evidence.reference_title: Genotype-phenotype relations for the Parkinson's disease genes SNCA, LRRK2, VPS35: MDSGene systematic review.
evidence.snippet: recapitulates many of the previously described findings including later onset of disease (median age at onset: ∼49 years) compared to recessive forms of PD of an overall excellent treatment response.

nodes.description: Fibrillar alpha-synuclein accumulates as cytoplasmic Lewy bodies and Lewy neurites, the pathological hallmark shared with sporadic Parkinson disease and dementia with Lewy bodies. In SNCA disease the burden is typically heavier and more widely distributed through cortex and limbic regions than in sporadic disease, and in the p.Gly51Asp and p.Ala53Glu subtypes it is accompanied by oligodendroglial glial cytoplasmic inclusions like those of multiple system atrophy. This node conforms to the module's Lewy-pathology anchor.
nodes.id: Lewy Body and Lewy Neurite Formation

evidence.reference_title: The new mutation, E46K, of alpha-synuclein causes Parkinson and Lewy body dementia.
evidence.snippet: The postmortem examination showed atrophy of the substantia nigra, lack of Alzheimer pathology, and numerous Lewy bodies which were immunoreactive to alpha-synuclein and ubiquitin in cortical and subcortical areas.

evidence.reference_title: Distinct clinical and neuropathological features of G51D SNCA mutation cases compared with SNCA duplication and H50Q mutation.
evidence.snippet: All three G51D cases had abundant α-synuclein pathology with characteristics of both PD and MSA. These included widespread cortical and subcortical neuronal α-synuclein inclusions together with small numbers of inclusions resembling glial cytoplasmic inclusions (GCIs) in oligodendrocytes.

nodes.description: Orthostatic hypotension from autonomic failure is managed with non-pharmacological measures and, when needed, agents such as midodrine, droxidopa or fludrocortisone, as in sporadic disease with dysautonomia.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal dominant Parkinson's disease caused by SNCA duplications.

nodes.description: Alpha-synuclein associates directly with mitochondrial membranes and fragments them; the effect is specific to alpha-synuclein over its beta and gamma isoforms, is independent of the fission GTPase Drp1, and is driven by the small oligomeric species. Fragmentation is followed by a decline in respiration and neuronal death. The node conforms to the module's mitochondrial-stress anchor, with alpha-synuclein membrane fragmentation as the disease-specific mechanism in place of complex I inhibition.

evidence.reference_title: Direct membrane association drives mitochondrial fission by the Parkinson disease-associated protein alpha-synuclein.
evidence.snippet: We now show that the expression of α-synuclein in mammalian cells, including neurons in vitro and in vivo, causes the fragmentation of mitochondria.

evidence.reference_title: Direct membrane association drives mitochondrial fission by the Parkinson disease-associated protein alpha-synuclein.
evidence.snippet: However, mitochondrial fragmentation is eventually followed by a decline in respiration and neuronal death.

nodes.description: Progressive, selective loss of dopaminergic neurons of the substantia nigra pars compacta, with relative sparing of the adjacent ventral tegmental area. In SNCA disease the loss follows from aggregation, impaired degradation, mitochondrial failure and transmitted pathology, and is often more severe and accompanied by wider cortical degeneration than in sporadic disease.

evidence.reference_title: Pathological α-synuclein transmission initiates Parkinson-like neurodegeneration in nontransgenic mice.
evidence.snippet: Lewy pathology accumulation resulted in progressive loss of dopamine neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta, but not in the adjacent ventral tegmental area, and was accompanied by reduced dopamine levels culminating in motor deficits.

evidence.reference_title: The new mutation, E46K, of alpha-synuclein causes Parkinson and Lewy body dementia.
evidence.snippet: The postmortem examination showed atrophy of the substantia nigra, lack of Alzheimer pathology, and numerous Lewy bodies which were immunoreactive to alpha-synuclein and ubiquitin in cortical and subcortical areas.

nodes.description: Postural fall in blood pressure from autonomic failure, part of the dysautonomia.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal dominant Parkinson's disease caused by SNCA duplications.
evidence.snippet: severe dysautonomia, including orthostatic hypotension with fainting

nodes.description: The cardinal motor syndrome, bradykinesia with rigidity, resting tremor and postural instability, produced by the striatal dopamine deficit and responsive to dopaminergic treatment. It is the shared clinical endpoint of every SNCA lesion.

evidence.reference_title: Distinct clinical and neuropathological features of G51D SNCA mutation cases compared with SNCA duplication and H50Q mutation.
evidence.snippet: Examination revealed tongue tremor, moderate bilateral resting hand tremor, bradykinesia, cogwheel rigidity, hyperreflexia and postural instability.

nodes.description: Impaired postural reflexes, a cardinal sign appearing as the disease advances.

evidence.reference_title: Distinct clinical and neuropathological features of G51D SNCA mutation cases compared with SNCA duplication and H50Q mutation.
evidence.snippet: Examination revealed tongue tremor, moderate bilateral resting hand tremor, bradykinesia, cogwheel rigidity, hyperreflexia and postural instability.

nodes.description: A single injection of synthetic alpha-synuclein fibrils into wild-type mouse striatum seeds the templated spread of Lewy pathology along connections, selectively kills nigral dopaminergic neurons, lowers striatal dopamine and produces motor deficits. The model recapitulates the propagation and selective degeneration steps of the cascade without any genetic lesion, so it isolates templated spread rather than modelling the SNCA genotype itself.
nodes.id: Preformed-fibril intrastriatal inoculation of wild-type mice (Luk et al.)

nodes.description: Misfolded fibrillar alpha-synuclein transfers between connected neurons and templates the aggregation of endogenous monomer in recipient cells. A single injection of synthetic fibrils into wild-type mouse striatum seeds Lewy pathology that spreads along anatomical connections, selectively kills nigral dopaminergic neurons and produces motor deficits, establishing that templated spread alone is sufficient to initiate the degenerative cascade.

animal_models.description: Templated cell-to-cell transmission of Lewy pathology along anatomical connections from a single fibril seed.

animal_models.name: Preformed-fibril intrastriatal inoculation of wild-type mice (Luk et al.)

evidence.reference_title: Pathological α-synuclein transmission initiates Parkinson-like neurodegeneration in nontransgenic mice.
evidence.snippet: we found that in wild-type nontransgenic mice, a single intrastriatal inoculation of synthetic α-Syn fibrils led to the cell-to-cell transmission of pathologic α-Syn and Parkinson's-like Lewy pathology in anatomically interconnected regions.

nodes.description: Resting tremor, a cardinal parkinsonian sign in SNCA carriers.

evidence.reference_title: Distinct clinical and neuropathological features of G51D SNCA mutation cases compared with SNCA duplication and H50Q mutation.
evidence.snippet: Examination revealed hypomimia, micrographia, bilateral resting hand tremor, asymmetrical bradykinesia and rigidity with parkinsonian gait and reduced arm swing.

nodes.description: Increased muscle tone, a cardinal parkinsonian sign.

evidence.reference_title: Distinct clinical and neuropathological features of G51D SNCA mutation cases compared with SNCA duplication and H50Q mutation.
evidence.snippet: Examination revealed tongue tremor, moderate bilateral resting hand tremor, bradykinesia, cogwheel rigidity, hyperreflexia and postural instability.

meta.association: Heterozygous missense variants in SNCA at 4q22, or duplication or triplication of the locus, cause autosomal dominant Parkinson disease. The gene encodes the 140-residue presynaptic protein alpha-synuclein, the main fibrillar constituent of Lewy bodies. p.Ala53Thr in the Contursi kindred and three Greek families (1997) was the first Mendelian cause of Parkinson disease found; locus triplication (2003) and duplication (2004) showed that an increased dose of the wild-type protein is sufficient.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation in the alpha-synuclein gene identified in families with Parkinson's disease.
evidence.snippet: A mutation was identified in the alpha-synuclein gene, which codes for a presynaptic protein thought to be involved in neuronal plasticity, in the Italian kindred and in three unrelated families of Greek origin with autosomal dominant inheritance for the PD phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Alpha-synuclein locus duplication as a cause of familial Parkinson's disease.
evidence.snippet: Genomic triplication of the alpha-synuclein gene (SNCA) has been reported to cause hereditary early-onset parkinsonism with dementia.

evidence.reference_title: Alpha-synuclein locus duplication as a cause of familial Parkinson's disease.
evidence.snippet: One kindred was identified with SNCA duplication by semiquantitative PCR and confirmed by fluorescent in-situ hybridisation analysis in peripheral leucocytes.

evidence.reference_title: SNCA / Parkinson disease (Definitive)
evidence.snippet: SNCA | HGNC:11138 | Parkinson disease | MONDO:0005180 | AD | Definitive

nodes.description: Three copies of the wild-type gene, with multiplicated intervals of variable size (about 0.9 Mb in the Swedish Lister family branch, average about 2 Mb across families) that may carry neighbouring genes such as MMRN1. Later onset than triplication, incomplete penetrance, and a phenotype ranging from idiopathic-like Parkinson disease to dementia with Lewy bodies and dysautonomia.

evidence.reference_title: Phenotypic variation in a large Swedish pedigree due to SNCA duplication and triplication.
evidence.snippet: Molecular analysis identified a genomic duplication of <0.9 Mb encompassing alpha-synuclein and multimerin 1 (SNCA-MMRN1), flanked by long interspersed repeat sequences (LINE L1).

evidence.reference_title: Causal relation between alpha-synuclein gene duplication and familial Parkinson's disease.
evidence.snippet: Two patients had duplications, which were confirmed by analysis of intragenic and flanking microsatellite markers. The phenotype in both patients was indistinguishable from idiopathic Parkinson's disease and no atypical features were present, by contrast with reports of families with triplication of the same gene.

nodes.description: Four copies of the wild-type gene (the Iowa kindred and a branch of the Swedish Lister family), doubling SNCA mRNA and alpha-synuclein protein in blood and brain. Fully penetrant, early-onset, rapidly progressive parkinsonism with dementia.

evidence.reference_title: Alpha-synuclein in blood and brain from familial Parkinson disease with SNCA locus triplication.
evidence.snippet: Here it is shown that SNCA triplication results in a doubling in the amount of alpha-synuclein protein in blood.

evidence.reference_title: Phenotypic variation in a large Swedish pedigree due to SNCA duplication and triplication.
evidence.snippet: The genetic basis for familial parkinsonism is an SNCA-MMRN11 multiplication, but whereas SNCA-MMRN1 duplication in the Swedish proband (Branch J) leads to late-onset autonomic dysfunction and parkinsonism, SNCA-MMRN1 triplication in the Swedish American family (Branch I) leads to early-onset Parkinson disease and dementia.

evidence.reference_title: Parkinson's disease induced pluripotent stem cells with triplication of the α-synuclein locus.
evidence.snippet: Triplication of SNCA, encoding α-synuclein, causes a fully penetrant, aggressive form of Parkinson's disease with dementia.

nodes.description: Induced pluripotent stem cells from an Iowa-kindred SNCA triplication patient and an unaffected first-degree relative, differentiated to midbrain dopaminergic neurons. Patient neurons make double the alpha-synuclein of the relative's, reproducing the dosage lesion in human neurons of the affected type and providing a platform for synuclein-lowering screens.
nodes.id: SNCA triplication patient iPSC-derived midbrain dopaminergic neurons (Devine et al.)

nodes.description: Loss of nigral terminals and the presynaptic release deficit together lower dopamine in the striatum, disrupting basal ganglia motor circuits and producing the cardinal motor signs. This is the pharmacological target of levodopa, which is why the disease, whatever its genetic cause, is levodopa-responsive. The node conforms to the module's striatal-deficit anchor.
nodes.id: Striatal Dopamine Deficiency and Basal Ganglia Circuit Dysfunction

evidence.reference_title: Pathological α-synuclein transmission initiates Parkinson-like neurodegeneration in nontransgenic mice.
evidence.snippet: was accompanied by reduced dopamine levels culminating in motor deficits.

nodes.description: Bilateral subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation benefits motor fluctuations and dyskinesia in selected SNCA carriers, with the best and most durable outcomes in duplication carriers who do not yet have cognitive decline; carriers with missense mutations and early dementia do less well and can deteriorate despite a motor benefit.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal dominant Parkinson's disease caused by SNCA duplications.
evidence.snippet: Thus, DBS might be potentially useful for selected SNCA duplication patients who have severe motor complications but do not have any cognitive deficits.

nodes.description: Visual hallucinations, the most consistently reported non-motor feature in duplication carriers and part of the dementia-with-Lewy-bodies-like picture of the more severe lesions.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal dominant Parkinson's disease caused by SNCA duplications.
evidence.snippet: Hallucinations were the only feature present significantly more often than not (χ2 test, p<0.01) in these patients.

nodes.description: Found in a German family in 1998. The substitution disrupts membrane association and synaptic enrichment of the protein; unlike the other alleles it does not inhibit synaptic vesicle exocytosis when overexpressed, and it fibrillizes more slowly, which may underlie its later onset and incomplete penetrance.

evidence.reference_title: Accelerated in vitro fibril formation by a mutant alpha-synuclein linked to early-onset Parkinson disease.
evidence.snippet: We demonstrate here that both mutant forms of alpha-synuclein (A53T and A30P) are, like wild-type alpha-synuclein (WT), disordered in dilute solution.

evidence.reference_title: Increased expression of alpha-synuclein reduces neurotransmitter release by inhibiting synaptic vesicle reclustering after endocytosis.
evidence.snippet: Consistent with a crucial role for the N-terminal membrane-binding domain, the PD-associated A30P mutation abolishes the inhibition of transmitter release by αsyn.

nodes.description: c.158C>A, found in a Finnish family. Atypical early-onset parkinsonism with neuropathology showing features of both multiple system atrophy and Parkinson disease, including oligodendroglial inclusions.

evidence.reference_title: Novel α-synuclein mutation A53E associated with atypical multiple system atrophy and Parkinson's disease-type pathology.
evidence.snippet: The A53E mutation was found in 2 other relatives who had parkinsonism. Our results suggest that the novel SNCA A53E substitution is a causative mutation resulting clinically in parkinsonism and pathologically in severe multiple system atrophy- and PD-type phenotype.

nodes.description: c.209G>A (G209A), the founding allele in the Contursi (Italian) and Greek kindreds, which share a haplotype; it also occurs de novo (Sweden) and on a different haplotype in Korea. Early-onset, severe, levodopa-responsive disease with prominent cortical dysfunction, dysphasia and cognitive decline in the Swedish family; incomplete penetrance in Greek families. Mutant protein fibrillizes fastest of the early alleles in vitro.

evidence.reference_title: A Swedish family with de novo alpha-synuclein A53T mutation: evidence for early cortical dysfunction.
evidence.snippet: Two affected individuals had early-onset (before 31 and 40 years), severe levodopa-responsive PD with prominent dysphasia, dysarthria, and cognitive decline.

evidence.reference_title: Mutated alpha-synuclein gene in two Greek kindreds with familial PD: incomplete penetrance?
evidence.snippet: The G209A mutation in the alpha-synuclein gene has been associated with autosomal dominant PD (ADPD) in a family from Contursi, Italy, and three apparently unrelated Greek families.

evidence.reference_title: Accelerated in vitro fibril formation by a mutant alpha-synuclein linked to early-onset Parkinson disease.
evidence.snippet: However, at higher concentrations, Lewy body-like fibrils and discrete spherical assemblies are formed; most rapidly by A53T.

nodes.description: Found in a Spanish (Basque) family with autosomal dominant parkinsonism, dementia and visual hallucinations, with cortical and subcortical Lewy bodies at autopsy; carriers show early cognitive impairment with a posterior cortical pattern, cardiac sympathetic denervation and small fibre neuropathy with dermal phosphorylated alpha-synuclein.

evidence.reference_title: The new mutation, E46K, of alpha-synuclein causes Parkinson and Lewy body dementia.
evidence.snippet: Sequencing of the alpha-synuclein gene showed a novel, nonconservative E46K mutation in heterozygosis.

evidence.reference_title: The new mutation, E46K, of alpha-synuclein causes Parkinson and Lewy body dementia.
evidence.snippet: The E46K mutation was present in all affected family members and in three young asymptomatic subjects, but it was absent in healthy and pathological controls.

nodes.description: c.152G>A, found in French and British kindreds. Early-onset parkinsonian-pyramidal syndrome with moderate levodopa response, rapid progression, psychiatric symptoms, dementia and autonomic failure, and neuropathology combining Lewy pathology with oligodendroglial inclusions like those of multiple system atrophy. Unlike most alleles it attenuates aggregation and membrane binding in vitro, while its fibrils are more toxic.

evidence.reference_title: G51D α-synuclein mutation causes a novel parkinsonian-pyramidal syndrome.
evidence.snippet: We identified a novel SNCA G51D (c.152 G>A) mutation that cosegregated with the disease and was absent from controls.

evidence.reference_title: α-Synucleinopathy associated with G51D SNCA mutation: a link between Parkinson's disease and multiple system atrophy?
evidence.snippet: We report a British family with young-onset Parkinson's disease (PD) and a G51D SNCA mutation that segregates with the disease.

nodes.description: Found in a patient with dopa-responsive Parkinson disease and a family history of parkinsonism and dementia; the clinical picture mimics late-onset idiopathic disease with a sustained levodopa response and typical Lewy pathology without glial inclusions. The mutant accelerates aggregation in vitro.

evidence.reference_title: Alpha-synuclein p.H50Q, a novel pathogenic mutation for Parkinson's disease.
evidence.snippet: Here, we describe a novel missense mutation in exon 4 of SNCA encoding a H50Q substitution in a patient with dopa-responsive Parkinson's disease with a family history of parkinsonism and dementia.

evidence.reference_title: The Parkinson's disease-associated H50Q mutation accelerates α-Synuclein aggregation in vitro.
evidence.snippet: Here, we analyzed the aggregation of newly discovered α-Syn missense mutant H50Q in vitro and found that this mutation significantly accelerates the aggregation and amyloid formation of α-Syn.
